decisions.rationale: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a single named disease with one specific definition, appearing in the title as a standalone disease mention.
The phrase refers to two separate diseases, Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy, joined in one contiguous string, so it is a Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 - Contiguous text strings (Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: The word 'disease' is a very general term and is excluded by the guidelines.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 - General terms

decisions.rationale: 'mdx' names a mouse mutation or strain rather than a disease name, so it does not qualify as a disease mention under the guidelines.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 - Organism names and related non-disease designations

decisions.rationale: 'dystrophic syndrome' is a vague descriptive phrase built on the general term 'syndrome', which the guidelines exclude as a general term.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 - General terms

decisions.rationale: 'Duchenne / Becker muscular dystrophy' refers to two separate diseases, Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy, in one contiguous string, so it is a Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 - Contiguous text strings (Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: Here 'Duchenne muscular dystrophy' is used as a modifier of the noun phrase 'gene' (the human Duchenne muscular dystrophy gene), so it is a Modifier rather than a standalone disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 - Disease mentions used as Modifiers

decisions.rationale: The abbreviation 'DMD' is a separate synonymous mention of the disease and modifies the noun 'gene' in 'DMD gene', so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6 - Synonymous mentions; What to Annotate 3 - Modifiers

decisions.rationale: 'DMD' is used as a disease-derived name modifying 'gene' in 'the gene homologous to DMD' (the locus/gene named after the disease), so it functions as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 - Disease mentions used as Modifiers

decisions.rationale: 'myopathies' refers to a family of multiple distinct diseases, so it is a Disease Class mention.
Emery Dreifuss muscular dystrophy is one specific named disease with a single definition and no further categorization.
'DMD' is the abbreviation of the disease used as a modifier of the noun 'homologue' in 'the DMD homologue', so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 - Disease mentions used as Modifiers; What to Annotate 6 - Synonymous mentions
